messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a burst of ECC/Xid alerts in us-west2 over the last hour, lots of transient single-sample spikes causing drains. Proposing a bounded 'quiet window' + batch coalescing so we only escalate when a card has >N events within M seconds or a sustained 2-min failure rate. Thoughts?
sophia: Can you paste the alert flood numbers? Is this across MIG or full-card?
alex: Most on full-card nodes, a handful on MIG instances. Snapshot: 24 cards reported Xid within 10m, 18 were single-sample spikes. Only 3 had repeated Xid within 5m.
raj: What about current Prom rules? We have one that fires on any DCGM ECC/Xid > 0 for 1m, which is too noisy.
alex: Exactly. Draft rule idea: use recording rule to compute per-card rolling count over 5m and a derivative to detect streaks. Then alert if count >=3 in 5m OR rate >0.5/min for 2m.
tara: Would prefer suppressing drains for single-sample events. Could we gate drains by score >= threshold and only auto-drain when score>5?
sophia: Score-based approach good. Also add a short 'quiet window' that suppresses repeat alerts for that card for 10m after a soft-warning so operators can triage.
alex: ```
# recording
record: dcgm_card_xid_count_5m
expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc.xid_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[5m])

# alerting
alert: GPUCardXidNoisy
expr: (
  dcgm_card_xid_count_5m >= 3
) or (
  increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc.xid_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[2m]) / 2 > 0.5
)
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  summary: "Noisy Xid on {{ $labels.card }}"
  description: "Card {{ $labels.card }} saw {{ $value }} Xid events"
```
raj: Prefer using `card_uid` label and a recording for 'single_sample' filter e.g., max_over_time(dcgm_gpu_ecc.xid_total[1m]) - ignoring noise.
tara: Edge cases: kernel recovers vs ECC memory errors. For ECC we should correlate with machine-level hwmon/thermal and host kernel logs before draining.
infra-bot: automated note: last runbook search 'dcgm noisy xid' returned playbook v2.1 — https://internal/redwood/runbooks/gpu-noise
sophia: Also consider regional constraints: us-west2 has low spare capacity — prefer marking node 'degraded' and ticketing RMA rather than immediate drain to avoid capacity impact.
alex: Agreed. Proposed action items: 1) Push recording rule to staging dashboards, 2) Create transient-suppression silence on alertmanager for single-sample > 10m, 3) adjust auto-drain policy to require score >=5 OR repeated alerts across 3 intervals. I'll PR rule later.
raj: :thumbsup: add unit tests for promql, and add alertmanager runbook links.
tara: I'll coordinate with support to make sure we don't break MIG nodes.
sophia: If everyone's OK I'll file the PR after lunch.
